title: Polymeric dimethylytterbium and the terminal methyl complex (Tp^{tBu,Me})Yb(CH3)(thf)

synthesis.procedure: Prepared under the conditions of a modified Lochmann route from bright yellow YbI2(thf)2 and 1.95 equivalents of K[N(SiMe3)2] in THF, followed by recrystallisation. Residual iodine persisted (ICP-OES and potentiometric titration). A separate SI micro-scale protonolysis of [YbMe2]n with HN(SiMe3)2 in [D8]THF also returned this amide.

reagents.name: ytterbium(II) iodide bis(tetrahydrofuran)
reagents.amount: not quantified in the main text

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: several recrystallisation steps; residual iodine remained

properties.summary: A UV-visible spectrum of the red-orange THF adduct is shown in the SI (n-hexane) together with the donor-free dimer; no absorption maxima are tabulated.

material_class.structural_family: dinuclear ytterbium(II) bis(trimethylsilyl)amide with bridging amides

synthesis.procedure: Under argon in a glovebox, HN(SiMe3)2 (467 mg, 2.8 mmol, 0.6 mL) in Et2O (2 mL) was added slowly to a suspension of [Yb(CH2Ph)2]n (1, 514 mg, 1.4 mmol) in Et2O (8 mL) and stirred overnight at ambient temperature. After filtration the solvent was removed under reduced pressure and the product was recrystallised from n-hexane as red crystals. Toluene is the only side product and is removed in vacuo.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration, solvent removal in vacuo, recrystallisation from n-hexane

properties.summary: The main text refers to a UV-visible spectrum of red-orange dimeric 2; the SI shows the spectrum in n-hexane without tabulated maxima.

material_class.structural_family: amorphous polymeric homoleptic dimethyl ytterbium, residual THF

synthesis.procedure: Method a, under argon. Chloride-free methyllithium (3.23 mL, 0.45 M, 1.46 mmol) in Et2O was added slowly with vigorous stirring to Yb[N(SiMe3)2]2(thf)2 (490 mg, 0.768 mmol) in Et2O (8 mL). An orange powder precipitated after about two-thirds of the MeLi had been added. The solvent was removed by filter cannula, and the solid was washed with Et2O (3 × 2 mL) and dried under vacuum. The product is oxygen- and water-sensitive and insoluble in aliphatic and aromatic solvents; ICP-OES iodine was 2.03%.

reagents.name: methyllithium
reagents.amount: 3.23 mL of 0.45 M Et2O solution, 1.46 mmol

synthesis.vessel_or_method: Et2O solution, vigorous stirring, filter cannula
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: precipitation of amorphous orange powder; wash with Et2O (3 × 2 mL); vacuum drying; not crystallised

synthesis.procedure: Method b follows method a under argon. Methyllithium in Et2O (5.2 mL, 0.31 M, 1.6 mmol) was combined with THF-free [Yb{N(SiMe3)2}2]2 (400 mg, 0.42 mmol) in Et2O (8 mL) to give orange [YbMe2]n, which was dried under high vacuum for 3 h. Iodine impurity was 0.39% (ICP-OES). The solid is amorphous; neither crystalline [YbMe2]n nor a crystalline THF adduct was obtained.

reagents.amount: 5.2 mL of 0.31 M Et2O solution, 1.6 mmol

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: orange amorphous powder; high-vacuum drying for 3 h; no single crystals

synthesis.procedure: Isolated on one occasion as orange single crystals while attempting to crystallise [YbMe2]n or a THF adduct. No deliberate stoichiometric procedure, amounts, or yield are given. The SI formulates the crystal as [Yb(II)6Yb(III)2(CH3)14O2(thf)6].
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: orange single crystals; structure determined by single-crystal XRD

synthesis.procedure: Under argon, HC5Me5 (20 mg, 0.15 mmol) in Et2O (3 mL) was added slowly with vigorous stirring to a suspension of [YbMe2]n (15 mg, 0.07 mmol) in Et2O (1 mL). The mixture was stirred for 18 h at 40 °C, filtered, concentrated to 1 mL, and stored at −40 °C to give bright green crystals.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration, concentration to 1 mL, storage at −40 °C

properties.summary: The SI shows a UV-visible spectrum of green (C5Me5)2Yb(Et2O) in n-hexane; no peak wavelengths are listed in the text.

material_class.structural_family: five-coordinate terminal Yb(II) methyl scorpionate; distorted square pyramid

synthesis.procedure: Main text: [YbMe2]n in THF was treated with 0.5 equivalents of HTp^{tBu,Me} to give a red solution of 6; more than 0.5 equivalents partly forms Yb(Tp^{tBu,Me})2. An equimolar reaction of 3 with Yb(Tp^{tBu,Me})2(OEt2) also gives 6 in good yield. SI, argon glovebox: HTp^{tBu,Me} (10.5 mg, 0.025 mmol) in THF (2 mL) was added dropwise to [YbMe2]n (10 mg, 0.05 mmol) in THF (1 mL) and stirred 20 min at ambient temperature until a clear red solution formed; filtration and concentration, then crystallisation from saturated THF at −40 °C. Alternatively, Yb(Tp^{tBu,Me})2 (60 mg, 0.06 mmol) in THF (0.4 mL) was added to [YbMe2]n (12 mg, 0.06 mmol) in THF (0.2 mL); after 15 min the solvent was evaporated to a red solid (67 mg, 84%). The solid darkens on prolonged vacuum or storage at ambient temperature. The crystal contains two molecules and lattice THF (CCDC formula C31H55BN6O1.5Yb).
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration and concentration; single crystals from saturated THF at −40 °C, or solvent evaporation
synthesis.yield: 67 mg, 84% for the Yb(Tp^{tBu,Me})2 route; protonolysis yield not stated

properties.summary: A UV-visible spectrum of red (Tp^{tBu,Me})Yb(CH3)(thf) in THF is shown in the SI; no numerical absorption maxima are reported in the text.
